guided.title: Monthly series for the line chart
guided.prompt: Print the data behind the line chart: one line per month in order, `month <m>: <net>` where net is the monthly net revenue from `net_month` (already prepared), formatted with 2 decimals. Then print `peak month: <m>` using `idxmax()`.
guided.starter:
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd


def generate(seed=7):
    """Seeded online-store data with planted defects: 500 orders, 120 customers, 20 products."""
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    customers = pd.DataFrame({
        "customer_id": np.arange(1, 121),
        "country": rng.choice(["DE", "FR", "UK", "US"], 120, p=[0.3, 0.2, 0.2, 0.3]),
        "signup_date": pd.Timestamp("2024-07-01") + pd.to_timedelta(rng.integers(0, 180, 120), unit="D"),
    })
    customers.loc[rng.choice(120, 8, replace=False), "country"] = "us "
    products = pd.DataFrame({
        "product_id": np.arange(1, 21),
        "category": np.repeat(["home", "beauty", "sports", "electronics"], 5),
        "unit_price": (10 + rng.random(20) * 90).round(2),
    })
    campaigns = pd.DataFrame({
        "campaign_id": [0, 1, 2, 3],
        "channel": ["organic", "email", "paid_search", "social"],
        "spend": [0.0, 800.0, 2500.0, 1200.0],
    })
    n = 500
    orders = pd.DataFrame({
        "order_id": np.arange(1001, 1001 + n),
        "customer_id": rng.integers(1, 121, n),
        "product_id": rng.integers(1, 21, n),
        "order_date": pd.Timestamp("2025-01-01") + pd.to_timedelta(rng.integers(0, 180, n), unit="D"),
        "quantity": rng.integers(1, 5, n),
        "discount_pct": rng.choice([0, 10, 20], n, p=[0.6, 0.25, 0.15]),
        "campaign_id": rng.choice([0, 1, 2, 3], n, p=[0.4, 0.2, 0.25, 0.15]),
    })
    orders.loc[rng.choice(n, 5, replace=False), "quantity"] = -1
    orders.loc[rng.choice(n, 6, replace=False), "customer_id"] = 999
    orders = pd.concat([orders, orders.sample(10, random_state=1)], ignore_index=True)
    returned = rng.choice(np.arange(1001, 1001 + n), 60, replace=False)
    returns = pd.DataFrame({
        "order_id": np.concatenate([returned, [9001, 9002, 9003]]),
        "reason": rng.choice(["damaged", "wrong_item", "changed_mind"], 63, p=[0.3, 0.2, 0.5]),
    })
    return {"orders": orders, "customers": customers, "products": products, "campaigns": campaigns, "returns": returns}



def clean(t):
    """Apply the quality rules; return cleaned tables and a row-accounting log."""
    log = {}
    o = t["orders"]
    log["raw_orders"] = len(o)
    o = o.drop_duplicates()
    log["after_duplicates"] = len(o)
    o = o[o["quantity"] > 0]
    log["after_quantity"] = len(o)
    c = t["customers"].copy()
    c["country"] = c["country"].str.strip().str.upper()
    o = o[o["customer_id"].isin(c["customer_id"])]
    log["after_customers"] = len(o)
    r = t["returns"]
    log["raw_returns"] = len(r)
    r = r[r["order_id"].isin(o["order_id"])].drop_duplicates("order_id")
    log["clean_returns"] = len(r)
    p = t["products"]
    o = o.merge(p[["product_id", "unit_price"]], on="product_id", how="left")
    o["revenue"] = (o["quantity"] * o["unit_price"] * (1 - o["discount_pct"] / 100)).round(2)
    o["returned"] = o["order_id"].isin(r["order_id"])
    return {"orders": o.reset_index(drop=True), "customers": c, "products": p, "campaigns": t["campaigns"], "returns": r.reset_index(drop=True)}, log



def prepare(ct):
    """Analysis tables from the clean data: orders with category, channel and month, plus the three chart series."""
    o = ct["orders"].merge(ct["products"][["product_id", "category"]], on="product_id")
    o = o.merge(ct["campaigns"][["campaign_id", "channel"]], on="campaign_id")
    o["month"] = o["order_date"].dt.month
    net = o[~o["returned"]]
    net_month = net.groupby("month")["revenue"].sum().round(2)
    spend = ct["campaigns"].set_index("channel")["spend"]
    roas = (net.groupby("channel")["revenue"].sum() / spend[spend > 0]).dropna().round(2)
    rate = (o.groupby("category")["returned"].mean() * 100).round(1)
    return o, net_month, roas, rate


ct, log = clean(generate())
o, net_month, roas, rate = prepare(ct)

    orders.loc[rng.choice(n, 6, replace=False), "customer_id"] = 999
    orders = pd.concat([orders, orders.sample(10, random_state=1)], ignore_index=True)
    returned = rng.choice(np.arange(1001, 1001 + n), 60, replace=False)
    returns = pd.DataFrame({
        "order_id": np.concatenate([returned, [9001, 9002, 9003]]),
        "reason": rng.choice(["damaged", "wrong_item", "changed_mind"], 63, p=[0.3, 0.2, 0.5]),

    """Apply the quality rules; return cleaned tables and a row-accounting log."""

    o = t["orders"]

    log["after_duplicates"] = len(o)
    o = o[o["quantity"] > 0]
    log["after_quantity"] = len(o)
    c = t["customers"].copy()

    o = o[o["customer_id"].isin(c["customer_id"])]
    log["after_customers"] = len(o)
    r = t["returns"]
    log["raw_returns"] = len(r)
    r = r[r["order_id"].isin(o["order_id"])].drop_duplicates("order_id")
    log["clean_returns"] = len(r)
    p = t["products"]
    o = o.merge(p[["product_id", "unit_price"]], on="product_id", how="left")
    o["revenue"] = (o["quantity"] * o["unit_price"] * (1 - o["discount_pct"] / 100)).round(2)
    o["returned"] = o["order_id"].isin(r["order_id"])
    return {"orders": o.reset_index(drop=True), "customers": c, "products": p, "campaigns": t["campaigns"], "returns": r.reset_index(drop=True)}, log



def prepare(ct):
    """Analysis tables from the clean data: orders with category, channel and month, plus the three chart series."""
    o = ct["orders"].merge(ct["products"][["product_id", "category"]], on="product_id")

    net = o[~o["returned"]]
    net_month = net.groupby("month")["revenue"].sum().round(2)
    spend = ct["campaigns"].set_index("channel")["spend"]
    roas = (net.groupby("channel")["revenue"].sum() / spend[spend > 0]).dropna().round(2)
    rate = (o.groupby("category")["returned"].mean() * 100).round(1)
    return o, net_month, roas, rate

for country, df in o.groupby("country"):

independent.solution:
Relationships: `Customers[customer_id]` to `Sales[customer_id]`, `Products[product_id]` to `Sales[product_id]` and `Calendar[date]` to `Sales[order_date]`, each one-to-many with the dimension on the one side and the Sales table on the many side. Mark `Calendar` as the date table.

Measures: `Gross Revenue = SUMX ( Sales, Sales[quantity] * Sales[unit_price] * ( 1 - Sales[discount_pct] / 100 ) )`; `Net Revenue = CALCULATE ( [Gross Revenue], Sales[returned] = FALSE () )`; `Orders = COUNTROWS ( Sales )`; `Return Rate = DIVIDE ( CALCULATE ( [Orders], Sales[returned] = TRUE () ), [Orders] )`.

Visuals: three cards (Net Revenue, Orders, Return Rate); a line chart with `Calendar[month_name]` on the axis and Net Revenue as the value; a bar chart with `Products[category]` on the axis and Return Rate as the value, sorted descending; a slicer on `Customers[country]`. Titles and axis titles are set on every visual.

Expected cards with no selection: Net Revenue 52630.99, Orders 489, Return Rate 12.1%. With the slicer on DE: 14001.03, 135 and 12.6%.
rubric: Relationships go from dimensions (one) to Sales (many).
Measures handle net revenue and return rate.
Visuals use the right fields, sorted and titled.
Expected values match the verified pandas results.

environment.note: The matplotlib and plotly examples run on your computer (they are shown read-only in the browser) and print figure properties instead of images. Power BI Desktop is Windows software and cannot run here: the Power BI page is given as steps and DAX, and every number it shows is verified with pandas. The graded exercises use pandas and plain Python.

checks.question: Which chart suits monthly net revenue over six months?
options: Line chart, because the order of months matters
checks.explanation: A trend over ordered time is a line. A pie hides the order, and a bar baseline above zero exaggerates differences.

checks.question: Why must a bar chart's y axis start at zero?
options: Bar length encodes the value, so a truncated axis exaggerates differences
checks.explanation: Readers compare bar lengths. If the axis starts at 8, the 8.7 bar looks almost empty next to the 14.5 bar, although the real ratio is about 0.6.

checks.question: How can a test verify a matplotlib chart without looking at it?
options: By printing properties such as the title, labels, bar heights and data behind the marks
By saving a PNG and comparing hashes in any environment
By counting the lines in the script
checks.explanation: Titles, labels and the data behind the marks are stable properties. Image bytes vary between machines and library versions.

checks.question: Why is return on spend not shown for organic?
options: Organic has zero spend, so the ratio is undefined
checks.explanation: Dividing by zero spend gives no meaningful ratio. Exclude it and note why, instead of showing infinity or zero.

checks.question: In the Power BI model, which relationship direction is standard?
checks.explanation: Dimension tables are on the one side, with unique keys, and the fact table is on the many side. Filters then flow from the dimension to the facts.
